description: 2 tactical challenges for White against the Rasa-Studier Gambit. Meet 3...e4 with 4.Nd4! or 5.Qc2!.

drills.briefExplanation: 3.Nf3 e4 4.Nd4! — centralize instead of allowing the pin.
drills.description: White to play. Black may push 3...e4 — develop and know the knight maneuver.
drills.explanation: The clean antidote: after 3...e4, White plays 4.Nd4! — centralizing before Black can pin with ...Bb4. The knight eyes c6 and e6, the e4 pawn is a target, and Black's whole gambit idea (pressure via the pin) never gets its trigger. Move order matters: Nd4 first, questions later.
drills.name: Nd4 Before Bb4

drills.briefExplanation: 3.Nf3 e4 4.Ng5 Bb4 5.Qc2! — defend c3 and prepare to break.
drills.description: White to play. Black pinned with 4...Bb4 — defend the knight with 5.Qc2!.
drills.explanation: If Black gets the pin in with 4...Bb4, White defends calmly: 5.Qc2! protects the c3 knight and prepares d3, breaking the e4 wedge. Black's pin looks scary but achieves little — White will untangle with a3 and d3, the extra tempo (Qc2 is useful anyway) keeps White in the game, and the gambit fizzles.
drills.name: The Qc2 Defense

name: Rasa-Studier Gambit — White Tactics
